chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the divorce of the intoxicated one, so he said: 'It is not valid, and there is no prestige (or: it is not considered a proper divorce).'
ai.seo_question: Is a divorce valid if pronounced by an intoxicated person in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ruled that the divorce pronounced by an intoxicated person is not valid (لا يجوز), emphasizing that it lacks the status or prestige of a valid divorce, meaning the marital bond remains intact or the divorce is considered null. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that 'sukr' (intoxication) impairs the mental capacity required for legal acts, distinguishing it from mere forgetfulness or minor distraction. The phrase 'wa la karamah' underscores the definitive nature of this nullity, ensuring clarity in family law regarding the status of the wife.
